source.title: ReMP: Low-Downtime Runtime Model-Parallelism Reconfiguration for LLM Serving
source.summary: Current large language model (LLM) inference systems universally deploy ultra-large-scale models using a combination of Tensor Parallelism (TP) and Pipeline Parallelism (PP). However, existing systems treat the model parallelism topology as a static configuration that cannot be flexibly adjusted at runtime. This rigid design creates a fundamental contradiction with the dynamically changing inference workloads in real-world scenarios. State-of-the-art systems lack online reconfiguration capabilities and can only switch configurations by restarting the service, resulting in several minutes of service interruption, KV cache loss, and prohibitive recomputation overhead. To address this problem, this paper presents ReMP, a runtime model parallelism reconfiguration framework that supports low downtime. ReMP achieves dynamic adjustment through three key techniques: (1) decoupling the model parallelism topology from runtime state to avoid full service reconstruction; (2) designing a two-dimensional KV cache migration mechanism to preserve reusable cache states after TP/PP changes; and (3) implementing end-to-end online reconfiguration. Experiments demonstrate that ReMP can complete most topology switches within 1-7 seconds on models ranging from 7B to 70B parameters, achieving speedups of tens to over a hundred times compared to the restart approach. Moreover, ReMP significantly outperforms fixed configurations under dynamic workloads, delivering superior performance in terms of TTFT, TPOT, and output throughput.

previous_facts.problem: Current LLM inference systems treat model parallelism topology (TP/PP) as static configuration, which conflicts with dynamically changing inference workloads. State-of-the-art systems lack online reconfiguration capabilities and can only switch configurations by restarting the service, resulting in several minutes of service interruption, KV cache loss, and prohibitive recomputation overhead.
previous_facts.mechanism: ReMP achieves dynamic TP/PP adjustment through three key techniques: (1) decoupling model parallelism topology from runtime state to avoid full service reconstruction; (2) two-dimensional KV cache migration mechanism to preserve reusable cache states after TP/PP changes; (3) end-to-end online reconfiguration using shared-memory model reloading, prebuilt parallel-state snapshots, and worker reuse.

evidence.claim: ReMP completes most topology switches within 1-7 seconds on models ranging from 7B to 70B parameters
evidence.baseline: restart-based approach (several minutes of service interruption)
evidence.condition: on H100 and RTX 5090 platforms, for Llama2-7B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, and Llama2-70B (excluding 4-GPU topologies for 70B)

evidence.claim: ReMP achieves speedups of tens to over a hundred times compared to restart approach
evidence.condition: model-parallel topology transitions on H100 platform

evidence.claim: ReMP outperforms fixed configurations under dynamic workloads in TTFT, TPOT, and output throughput
evidence.condition: under dynamic request pressure using BurstGPT-derived request traces

evidence.claim: Experimental hardware platforms: 8x NVIDIA H100 GPUs with AMD EPYC 7R13 CPU and 2TB RAM, or 8x NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPUs with Intel Xeon Gold 6530 CPU and 960GB RAM
Models evaluated: Llama2-7B, Llama2-70B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, Qwen3-30B-A3B
evidence.condition: dense and MoE architectures, Llama2-70B excluded from RTX 5090 due to GPU memory limits

previous_facts.evaluation_context: Experiments conducted on two 8-GPU platforms (H100 and RTX 5090) using four representative LLMs from 7B to 70B parameters. Workload uses BurstGPT-derived request traces replayed under different request pressures. Software implemented on vLLM V1. Comparisons made against restart-based reconfiguration baseline and fixed TP/PP configurations.
previous_facts.limitations: Llama2-70B not evaluated on RTX 5090 due to GPU memory limitations. Evidence pack focuses on single-node or cluster-level reconfiguration without WAN/cross-region deployment validation. Restart baseline defined qualitatively as 'several minutes' without explicit time measurements. No production deployment validation or multi-tenant isolation analysis. KV cache migration overhead visible but WAN RTT/bandwidth constraints not evaluated.
previous_facts.project_relevance: ReMP demonstrates KV cache migration across model parallelism topologies within a single cluster, but the paper focuses on TP/PP reconfiguration for adaptive serving rather than cross-region transmission. The two-dimensional KV cache migration mechanism may offer insights for remote KV cache access patterns, but WAN costs, compression, incremental transfer, and cross-region consistency are not addressed. Cache state preservation techniques could inform cross-region cache migration strategies, though this application is beyond the paper's scope.
source_notes: Evidence pack covers abstract, introduction, and evaluation sections (Pages 1-2, 9-10, 13)
